findings.affected_surface: Vimscript API: extend() / extendnew() built-in functions
findings.old_behavior: When dict_extend_func is called with a NULL second argument (expr2), the early-return at the d2==NULL check (old lines 1338-1340) exits before the is_new block and the rettv assignment. For extendnew() (is_new=true), d1 is never copied and rettv is left uninitialized. For extend() (is_new=false), the return value for the caller is also left unset.
findings.new_behavior: The d2==NULL check is moved after the is_new copy block. When d2 is NULL, execution jumps to the 'theend:' label which properly sets rettv: for extendnew() returns a copied dict, for extend() returns the original dict reference via copy_tv().
findings.compatibility_reason: The return value contract for extend() and extendnew() changed when the second argument is NULL. Previously the return value was undefined/uninitialized (a bug). Now it returns a proper copy (extendnew) or the original reference (extend). Vim scripts that passed a NULL second argument would previously get garbage; now they get a valid result. This is a bug fix but technically changes observable behavior for the NULL expr2 input case.
findings.why_not_internal_only: dict_extend_func is called from extend(), which is a public Vimscript built-in function (extend() and extendnew()). The return value of these functions is part of the user-visible Vimscript API surface.
findings.uncertainty: The old behavior was clearly a bug (returning with unset rettv). The practical compatibility impact is very low because no well-written Vim script would depend on getting undefined values from extendnew(). However, technically the return contract for the NULL expr2 case has changed.
findings.recommended_review: Verify that existing Vim scripts using extend()/extendnew() with test_null_dict() or NULL dicts still work correctly. The fix is backwards-compatible for all non-NULL inputs.
findings.test_recommendation: Run existing test_listdict.vim tests, particularly Test_listdict_extend and Test_listdict_extendnew. Add assertions for extendnew() with test_null_dict() to verify the return value is a valid copy.
